reader_guide: Read the overall grade as a judgment of the code in this checkout at Stage 1, not as approval for a public release. This is professional engineering with real tests and carefully drawn process boundaries. It is not AI slop. The first two refactors matter most: a slow History save can divert words away from the intended editor, and an unreadable polish setting silently turns off a feature the founder considers core. Each dimension gives one strong example and one finding you can check at the cited lines. Severity describes the effect on the founder’s phone today; confidence describes how firmly the code supports the finding. The three risk dimensions also name the phone test needed to settle behavior that source reading cannot prove. The roadmap orders changes so heart-path fixes come before cleanup. This was a read-only review: no build, Gradle task, or device test was run. The checkout has no root CLAUDE.md, and this was not a line-by-line review of every file in the inventory. Those limits reduce confidence in claims about the whole app, especially latency, lifecycle behavior, and the actual network payload.

overall_grade.rationale: This is professional Stage 1 Android engineering, not AI slop, but it is not yet production-grade for a wider release. The one-session design, process isolation, typed outcomes, privacy filtering, and outcome tests show senior work. History durability can still gate insertion, and a failed polish-policy read silently selects Off despite polish being core. A close race in language detection and allocation on the capture thread add smaller but concrete risks. AppShell is 240 lines and the Service shell is 253; the remaining mass is the 1,323-line coordinator and 997-line audio service.
overall_grade.confidence_rationale: The principal findings are directly visible in source, but the root CLAUDE.md is absent, not every priority file received a line-by-line review, and read-only constraints barred builds and phone tests.

dimensions.name: Architecture integrity
dimensions.justification: Six surfaces command one owner. The Service and AppShell have been split: the inventory measures DictationSessionService at 253 lines, AppShell at 240, and DictationSessionCoordinator at 1,323. The coordinator remains the largest owner, but its capture, polish, and finalization mechanics have named delegates. The material breach is that optional History persistence chooses whether the heart may attempt insertion.

dimensions.name: Concurrency discipline
dimensions.justification: Capture commands use a dedicated ordered lane, binder callbacks are posted to main, and service scopes are cancelled. A specific detector close race remains. The capture loop also allocates heartbeat events, against the project's strict capture-thread rule.

best_example.why_exemplary: The blocking cross-process operation is ordered and kept off main.

worst_violation.falsifiability: Use a controllable LanguageIdentifier seam. Pause detector A after its client CAS, let detector B obtain that client, call close, then resume A. This finding is wrong if B's client remains open until B exits.

dimensions.name: Performance and latency
dimensions.justification: Audio events and the recorder picture are pushed rather than polled. Model warm-up occurs off main. Static reading still shows a possible one-second History wait before insertion, plus settings preparation before capture. Measure accepted trigger to first frame, stop to visible text, and text to insertion on the S26 with History healthy, slow, and failed.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: The owner awaits the History result before the insertion handoff. The actual delay distribution requires measurement.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A slow History write adds up to the configured save bound before the user sees an insertion or clipboard result.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: The wait is in the publication continuation, immediately before commit and delivery.

dimensions.name: Security and privacy
dimensions.justification: Audio has no network path in the inspected pipeline, provider secrets use Keystore-backed AES-GCM, PostHog and Sentry have restrictive schemas, vendor prompt logging is silenced before inference, and model files are byte-counted and SHA-256 verified. The model URL revision check examines the whole URL rather than parsed path segments. The compiled catalog currently uses pinned paths, so this is a future-edit hole rather than evidence of an unsafe installed model. Capture and inspect actual outbound payloads and clipboard behavior on the S26 to settle the network boundary.

best_example.snippet:
fun sanitize(event: SentryEvent): SentryEvent {
        event.serverName = null
        event.request = null
        event.user = null
        event.transaction = null
        event.setModules(null)
        event.setUnknown(null)
        event.platform = event.platform?.let(SentrySchema::identifier)
best_example.why_exemplary: The send-time boundary clears free-form fields before a Sentry event leaves the process.

worst_violation.confidence_rationale: A URL query can satisfy contains even when its path omits the revision; the present catalog paths are correctly pinned and SHA-256 still guards the bytes.
worst_violation.counterfactual: A future catalog edit could pass availability with the revision only in a query string, hiding an unpinned source path. A wrong file would still fail the hash check.
worst_violation.counterfactual_rationale: contains checks all URL text, while the rule requires the revision in the source path.
worst_violation.falsifiability: Construct a ModelDescriptor with pinnedRevision abc and sourceUrl https://models.enviouslabs.co/a/b/file?note=/abc/. The finding is wrong if isAvailable rejects it.

refactor_targets.title: Let insertion proceed when History is slow or unavailable
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Give insertion a take-scoped identity independent of the Room row ID. Move the History save and reconciliation behind the insertion handoff in SessionFinalizer; keep a neutral row when persistence succeeds later. Make failure or timeout choose the same pinned-editor insertion route, with clipboard fallback only if that route fails.

refactor_targets.title: Distinguish a failed polish-policy read from Off
refactor_targets.rule_violated: .claude/rules/kotlin-patterns.md RULE: fail-open-to-the-last-good-text; named principle: distinguish failure from user choice
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Replace readPolicy's bare PolishPolicy return with a sealed Fresh or Failed result. Keep the last successful policy for the session; when none exists, use the declared local default. Carry Failed into TakePolishController so the deterministic text is published with the polish notice and one defect. Apply the same typed treatment to a null AIDL policy.

refactor_targets.title: Make ML Kit client release wait for all active detections
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Delete releaseClient from the post-CAS closed branch. Let that branch return null and let the existing final activeDetections decrement release the client only when the count reaches zero. Add a controlled two-detection close test for the stated interleaving.

refactor_targets.title: Remove heartbeat allocations from the capture loop
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Replace Event.Tick creation in offerTick with preallocated primitive heartbeat fields and an atomic pending flag consumed by TakeEventPublisher's worker. Keep object construction and queue nodes on that worker. Verify no allocation, logging, binder call, or contended lock occurs in the positive-read path.

refactor_targets.title: Move start preparation out of the session state machine
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Introduce a per-take SessionStartPreparation value and preparer below the coordinator. Move settings-answer timing, vocabulary matcher compilation, policy-read outcome, and journal-admission wait from beginSession into that preparer. Return one immutable result; leave the coordinator's state check, freeze, and binding decision in the owner.

refactor_targets.title: Remove the unwired model eviction policy
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: production policy must be wired or removed
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Delete ModelLifecyclePolicy.kt and its isolated ModelLifecyclePolicyTest until an actual model-residency control is designed and connected to ASR and polish service lifetimes.

refactor_targets.title: Narrow the legacy capture wait helper
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Mark AudioCaptureService.waitForFileReady private. Preserve the existing append-only AIDL method and its binder delegation for the separately installed instrumentation client.

refactor_targets.title: Validate model revision as a URL path segment
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Parse each source URL once with URI, validate its approved host, and require pinnedRevision as a complete path segment. Require a nonblank revision of the expected hash shape. Keep the existing exact byte-count and SHA-256 checks.

refactor_targets.title: Remove an assertion-free test
refactor_targets.rule_violated: Named engineering principle: a test must be able to fail
refactor_targets.fix_shape: Delete serviceLineCountIsReported from SessionOwnerShapeTest. Read sizes from the generated senior-audit inventory; keep the neighboring behavior and structure assertions as tests.

strengths.pattern_name: One Android shell with injected session seams
strengths.why_preserve: The service constructs adapters once and gives decisions to the coordinator.
A failed or silent reader yields a typed result and last successful values.
Invalid and blank remote answers fail open with a defect instead of holding the take.
The attempted-write record is set before the editor call, preventing a retry from duplicating text.
The decided hold plays silence, ends once, and releases its route.
Ready requires an exact file set, receipt, byte counts, and hashes in app-private storage.
Free-form fields are cleared and event messages are judged against a declared schema.
